identity.title: Left parasternal (RV) heave and loud/palpable P2

technique.how: Patient supine at 30-45 degrees. Place the heel of the hand over the left lower sternal border and feel for a sustained outward lift during systole (RV heave), then palpate the 2nd left interspace for a palpable P2. Auscultate the pulmonic area for a loud pulmonic component of S2, comparing intensity with A2, at rest and during a slow inspiration.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet room; patient not in acute respiratory distress that prevents breath control.

interpretation.positive_finding: A loud P2 modestly raises the probability of pulmonary hypertension (mPAP >=25 mmHg): LR+ 1.6 at rest and 1.9 on inspiration for all examiners, 3.2 when elicited by a specialist. An RV lift has LR+ about 1.1-1.3 and is essentially non-discriminating.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of either sign does not exclude pulmonary hypertension; all negative LRs were about 0.7-1.0 and no finding reliably ruled PH out.
interpretation.pitfalls: Sensitivity is low (21-43%) and generalist examiners performed no better than chance for these signs. A parasternal lift can also come from left atrial enlargement in mitral regurgitation or from a thin chest wall.
interpretation.changes_what: Loud P2 or RV heave: move to echocardiography for RV pressure and function. Absent signs should not lower suspicion of PH or PE when the history is suggestive.

estimates.reference_standard: Right heart catheterization, mean pulmonary artery pressure >=25 mmHg

sources.citation: Colman R, Whittingham H, Tomlinson G, Granton J. Utility of the physical examination in detecting pulmonary hypertension. A mixed methods study. PLoS One. 2014;9(10):e108499.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on these signs to exclude PH, RV failure or PE; do not use them to defer echo in a hypotensive or syncopal patient.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: RV heave or loud P2 with hypotension, syncope, or rising JVP suggests acute RV failure (massive PE, PH crisis) and needs immediate echo and escalation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No kappa reported. Specialists outperformed generalists: loud P2 on inspiration LR+ 3.2 (specialists) vs 1.2 (generalists); quote 'positive LR 1.2, 95% CrI [0.58, 2.4]' for generalists (Results text after Table 3).

extraction_notes: PMC OA full text of PMID 25343585 read; all five estimates copied from Table 3 (All Examiners and Specialists columns). Prevalence 25/52 = 0.481 computed from Results ('25 met criteria for PH'). Values are Bayesian credible intervals (CrI). The paper's systematic review (31 studies) found heterogeneous, mostly uncontrolled data; its Table 1 re-derives from a liver-transplant cohort of 55 patients (8 with PAH): quote 'a loud P2 had a sensitivity of 37.5% [95% CI: 14%-69%] and a specificity of 98% [95% CI: 89%-100%] while an RV heave had a sensitivity of 37.5%' (Results/Table 1 of review section). That primary study is cited only as reference [27] without a PMID I could confirm, so it is not entered as an estimate. No JAMA RCE exists for pulmonary hypertension exam. Generalist-only rows (LR+ 1.0-1.5) omitted as estimates but visible in Table 3.
